cards.title: THE GUEST BEDROOM
cards.tagline: THE ROOM WITH NO DAILY USER IS WHERE EVERYTHING UNDECIDED HIDES.
cards.objective: The guest bedroom is the only room in the house with no daily user, which is why it quietly absorbs whatever the rest of the house could not decide about. This card is the map.
zones_in_order: GBZ-005 Guest Welcome and Work Surface
cards.start_here: GBZ-004 Guest Closet. Open the closet first and pull everything onto the bed. You cannot judge how much room a visitor actually has while half of it is hidden behind a closet door, and working on the bed forces you to finish before anyone can sleep in here.
how_to_play: 1. Deal the five ZONE cards face up. Pick the one that is annoying you today, or take the one this card says to start at.
2. Lay out that zone's three FRICTION cards. Keep the ones that are true in your guest room. Put the rest back.
3. Turn a friction card over and pick the answer that is true. It names a ROOT CAUSE.
4. The root cause card names the ACTION cards that fix that cause. Pick the one that matches the time you actually have: fifteen or thirty minutes.
5. Do it standing up, with the card in your hand.
6. Read the victory condition out loud. If it is not true yet, you are not finished, and that is the whole scoring system.
7. Fill in the zone's STANDARD card with a pen and put it where the zone is.
8. Draw an EVENT card when an ordinary hard day happens, and see whether the standard held.
cards.players: 1 to 6. With more than one, deal the friction cards out and let each person keep the ones they believe. Disagreement is the useful part, not a problem to resolve before starting.
cards.six_s: Sort, Straighten, Shine, Safety, Standardize, Sustain
cards.safety_first: Do GBA-011 The Full Room Safety And Access Walk before any rebuild. It takes thirty minutes and covers the dark path, every cord, and the dresser strap.

the_call.title: The demoted sheets
the_call.text: The linen in this room got here because it stopped being good enough for your own bed. Thin sheets, the pilled set, the flat pillows, all quietly reassigned to people who will never say anything about it. The rule that settles it: if you would not sleep on it yourself for a week, it is not guest linen, it is cleaning cloth. Keep two complete sets that pass that test and let the rest go, even if it means buying one set. Two good sets beat six tired ones, and the shelf finally holds a decision instead of a backlog.

the_call.title: Two cables, tested
the_call.text: There are probably six or seven charging cables in this house that nobody can account for, and a few have drifted into this drawer on the theory that a guest might need one. They will not. A guest will find a cable, trust it because it is offered, plug in, and wake to a phone that never charged. That is worse than offering nothing. The rule: keep exactly two here, one of each connector your visitors actually carry, and prove each one tonight by charging a real device with it. Anything you cannot prove goes to the household charging drawer or into electronics recycling. An untested cable is not hospitality, it is a trap with a bow on it.

the_call.title: The overflow you told yourself was free
the_call.text: You have been storing things in here on the reasoning that the room stands empty most of the year, so the space costs nothing. It costs the whole point of the room. The rule: these two drawers belong to the guest and are never available, not for a week, not for the box you are about to sort properly, not for the winter coats until spring. When something in the house needs a home and this dresser is the only candidate, that is not a reason to take the drawer, it is a signal that you have not yet decided about the thing. Make the decision instead. This is the drawer that turns a storage room with a bed in it back into a guest room.

the_call.title: The box you have not opened since the move
the_call.text: There are two or three boxes on that shelf that were sealed at a previous address and have traveled unopened ever since. You keep them because opening one feels like it might cost an afternoon, and you keep meaning to have that afternoon. Do it standing here, now, with one box. If you can name a specific person and a specific occasion for what is inside, it earns a labeled home. If you find yourself saying we might need it, that is not a use, that is a delayed decision wearing a use's clothes. For anything you truly cannot face, write today's date on the lid in marker and put it back. If a year passes and you have not opened it again, it leaves unopened, and you will not remember what was in it.

safety_checks.text: An extension lead running from the desk across the open floor to the only reachable outlet, in the strip of carpet a guest walks in the dark.

safety_checks.question: Fall, cut, or crush

the_call.title: The room's second job
the_call.text: Almost every guest room is also something else: the home office, the sewing room, the place the exercise bike ended up. Pretending otherwise is precisely why hosting takes an afternoon, because you are not tidying, you are relocating an entire activity under time pressure. Name the second job out loud and give it a marked footprint, then test it honestly: can you clear that footprint into one bin or one cupboard, in a single trip, without unplugging anything? If yes, share the room and set the boundary in tape. If no, the second job is too big to share this room, and something moves out for good. That decision is uncomfortable, and it is the one that turns hosting from an event into a bed change.

cards.objective: The item is kept for what it represents, not because it is used, and the guilt stalls Sort indefinitely.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Ask if you would buy this again today for what it does. If the answer is no but you still cannot decide, the hold is sentimental.

cards.title: PERCEPTUAL BLINDNESS
cards.objective: The clutter has been visible so long the eye stops flagging it as a problem.
cards.confirm_in_30_seconds: Ask someone who does not live here to name what looks out of place. If they see it instantly and you had stopped noticing, this is the cause.

cards.title: TEST EVERY GUEST SET, RAG THE FAILURES
cards.objective: Take every sheet set that has been demoted to this room and try each fitted sheet on the actual mattress, so nothing that fails the test stays in the guest rotation.
cards.why_it_matters: A set that pops a corner mid-make is a rag, not a spare, and a guest has no way to know which one they were handed.
inputs: a bin bag or rag pile
steps: Take every sheet set that has been demoted to this room and try each fitted sheet on the actual mattress. If a corner pops off while you are making the bed, it is a rag, not a spare. Fold each pillow in half and let go, and anything that stays folded goes out.
Count what survives: you need exactly two complete sets for this bed, not however many happen to fit on the shelf.
cards.victory_condition: Every remaining sheet set has passed the mattress test, and every remaining pillow springs back when folded in half.

art.subject: a hand testing a fitted sheet's corner against a bare mattress, a folded rejected set set apart on the floor beside it
must_show: Every remaining sheet set has passed the mattress test, and every remaining pillow springs back when folded in half.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: CLEAR UNDER THE BED AND WALK THE DARK ROUTE
cards.objective: Empty anything that is not the guest suitcase out from under the bed, tie up any loose blind cord, and walk the route from pillow to door with the lights off.
cards.why_it_matters: A guest crossing this room in the dark has never memorised where the footstool or the box lives; you have, which is exactly why you cannot see the hazard anymore.
inputs: nothing beyond your own two feet and the lights switch
steps: Walk from the pillow to the door with the lights off, the way a guest will in the small hours in a room they do not know, and clear anything their shin will find.
If the bed sits under a blind, tie the cord up out of reach of a visiting toddler.
Remove anything from under the bed that is not the one folded-flat suitcase, and give it a real home elsewhere in the house.
cards.victory_condition: Nothing but one empty suitcase remains under the bed, and the dark walk from pillow to door meets no obstacle.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a hand tying up a blind cord above a guest bed at night, the floor path to the door visibly clear
must_show: Nothing but one empty suitcase remains under the bed, and the dark walk from pillow to door meets no obstacle.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: CLEAR THE DRAWER OF EVERYTHING THAT ISN'T A GUEST'S
cards.objective: Take out everything that has been hiding in this drawer and leave only what a guest actually needs.
cards.why_it_matters: None of what collects here belongs to a guest, and none of it belongs to you either once you actually look at it.
steps: Open the drawer and take out what has been hiding in a room nobody uses: dead batteries, a clock radio that lost its time when the power blipped, three paperbacks nobody chose, cough drops fused into their tin. None of it belongs to a guest, and none of it belongs to you either.
Leave only a card with the wifi name and password inside the empty drawer.
cards.victory_condition: The drawer holds only what a guest needs: a lamp within reach, two tested cables, tissues, a coaster and the wifi card, nothing of the household's.

art.subject: a hand clearing dead batteries and an old paperback out of a nightstand drawer, a single wifi card left inside
must_show: The drawer holds only what a guest needs: a lamp within reach, two tested cables, tissues, a coaster and the wifi card, nothing of the household's.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: PROVE TWO CABLES AND MOVE THE HAZARDS
cards.objective: Keep exactly two cables here, one of each connector your visitors actually carry, and prove each one tonight by charging a real device. Move any prescription or medicine out of the drawer.
cards.why_it_matters: An untested cable is not hospitality, it is a trap with a bow on it, and medicine at toddler height is a poisoning risk the moment a visiting family uses this room.
inputs: a real phone to test with
the two cables you are keeping
steps: Charge a real device from each cable you plan to keep before a guest ever tries either one.
Move anything of the household's, prescriptions and painkillers included, out of this drawer for good.
Confirm the lamp switch can be found by feel with the room dark.
cards.victory_condition: Two tested cables reach the pillow, the lamp switch is findable by feel in the dark, and nothing of the household's remains in the drawer.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a hand charging a phone from a nightstand cable in a dim room, the charge indicator lit
must_show: Two tested cables reach the pillow, the lamp switch is findable by feel in the dark, and nothing of the household's remains in the drawer.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: OPEN THE TOP DRAWERS AND MAKE THE DECISION
cards.objective: Clear the top two drawers of everything the household has been storing there, and make the one decision that has been avoided about the baby clothes.
cards.why_it_matters: This dresser is not free storage because the room stands empty most of the year; every week it holds the household's overflow is a week the guest room is not actually a guest room.
inputs: a marker for the drawer label
somewhere for the jumpers and cables to go
steps: This is where the household's undecided things hide behind a closed front: off-season jumpers, a bin of cables, wrapping paper and ribbon, a bag of outgrown baby clothes waiting on a decision about a second child. The jumpers go to your own wardrobe, the cables to the drawer that already holds cables, and the baby clothes get the decision today rather than another year of storage.
Label the inside front edge of a lower drawer with what it now holds.
cards.victory_condition: The top two drawers stand empty and lined, and the lower drawers hold only spare linens for this room's bed.

art.subject: a dresser's top drawer standing empty and lined, a bag of baby clothes set apart on the floor awaiting a decision

cards.objective: Fix an anti-tip strap between the dresser and the wall, and remove any loose plastic or dry-cleaning film from a low drawer.
cards.why_it_matters: An unstrapped dresser with heavy linens low and light drawers high is a real tip-over risk in a room where a visiting child is often left to play.
inputs: an anti-tip strap and its fixings
steps: Fix the anti-tip strap between the back of the dresser and the wall stud, not just the drywall.
Remove any dry-cleaning film or loose plastic bags from a low drawer a small guest could open.
Mark these two drawers reserved so nothing of the household's moves back in.

cards.title: OPEN THE SEALED BOX AND NAME A PERSON OR IT GOES
cards.objective: Empty this closet onto the bed and sort everything by whether a named person will use it in a named situation.
cards.why_it_matters: A box sealed since a previous address that nobody can name a use for is not storage, it is a decision wearing a use's clothes.
inputs: a marker for dating anything you cannot yet decide on
steps: Take everything out and put it on the bed. This closet is where the house keeps holiday decorations, a wedding dress in a zipped bag, a box of old phones, and paperwork from two addresses ago. Sort by whether a named person will use it in a named situation, and route the rest out.
For anything you truly cannot face today, write today's date on the lid and give yourself one year before it leaves unopened.
cards.victory_condition: At least a forearm's width of clear rod carries six matching empty hangers, and the floor square for a suitcase is clear.

steps: Move every heavy box off the shelf directly above the rod, and repack household storage into labeled lidded bins below head height.
Clear the closet floor of loose bins so a suitcase has a real square to sit in.
Stick a strip of tape on the rod marking exactly where the guest section ends.

cards.title: CLEAR THE DESK COMPLETELY
cards.objective: Clear the desk surface completely and send everything on it back to where it actually belongs.
cards.why_it_matters: Gift wrap, an ironing pile, and an unused printer are the household's second job spilling onto the one surface a guest needs clear.
inputs: the wardrobe the ironing came from
steps: Clear the surface completely. It will be holding gift wrap, an ironing pile that never made it back, a printer that has not been switched on this year, and paperwork someone brought in here to deal with in peace. The ironing goes back to the wardrobe it came from, the printer either earns a desk somewhere it gets used or leaves the house, and the paperwork goes into the file it was always headed for.
cards.victory_condition: The desk stands clear with a working lamp, and no cord crosses the walking line to the outlet.

cards.title: GIVE THE SECOND JOB A MARKED FOOTPRINT AND MOVE THE CORD
cards.objective: Name this room's second job out loud, give it a marked footprint you can clear in one trip, and route the extension lead away from the walking path.
cards.why_it_matters: Pretending this room has only one job is why hosting takes an afternoon; naming the second job honestly is what turns it back into a bed change.
inputs: one bin or cupboard for the second job
steps: Name the room's second job out loud, and test it: can the whole thing clear into one bin or one cupboard, in a single trip, without unplugging anything?
Mark that footprint in tape so the boundary is visible, not assumed.
Move the extension lead so it no longer crosses the floor a guest walks in the dark.
cards.victory_condition: The second job clears into its marked footprint in one trip, and no cord crosses the walking line to the outlet.

cards.title: THE FULL ROOM SAFETY AND ACCESS WALK
cards.objective: Walk the whole room testing what a guest cannot see for themselves: the lamp switch in the dark, every cord's route, and whether anything about this room's own habits has gone unnoticed for too long.
cards.why_it_matters: You know this room too well to see its own hazards; a guest meets all of them for the first time, in the dark, tonight.
inputs: nothing beyond the lights switch and your own hands
steps: With the lights off, find the nightstand lamp switch by feel alone, the way a guest will.
Walk every cord in the room and confirm none of them crosses a path a guest would take.
Ask someone who does not live here to name one thing about this room that looks out of place to them; if they see it instantly and you had stopped noticing, fix that thing first.

cards.title: WHO WALKS THIS ROOM BEFORE A GUEST ARRIVES

cards.title: THE MONTHLY BORROWED-SPACE AUDIT

inputs: nothing beyond the boundaries you have already marked
steps: Check the top two dresser drawers are still empty and the closet's tape line still marks a real boundary.
Check the desk's marked footprint still holds only what it was given.
For anything that has crept back in, decide today where it actually belongs rather than let it stay.
cards.victory_condition: Every marked boundary in this room, the drawers, the closet line, and the desk footprint, still holds exactly what it was given, checked this month.

art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: GUEST BED AND LINENS STANDARD
cards.tagline: WRITE IT. SIGN IT. PUT IT WHERE IT HAPPENS.
cards.objective: Two complete guest sets, each bundled in its own pillowcase and tagged with the bed size, and one of them always on the bed.
cards.trigger: When you carry the departing guest's towels to the machine, the sheets come off the bed and go in with them.
cards.instruction: This is a write on card. Fill it in with a pen, in your own words if the printed sentence is not yours, and put it where the zone is. A standard nobody signed is a preference.
micro_quest: Run the vacuum's upholstery tool along the mattress seams where dust settles between guests.
Wipe the headboard's top edge with a dry microfiber cloth, the one strip nobody's arm ever reaches while sitting up.
Pull the bed a stride from the wall and vacuum the strip of floor behind it.

art.subject: a made-up guest bed with a mattress protector and one complete sheet set, a second folded set with a visible size tag standing on a shelf nearby, two pillows resting beside it, and one empty suitcase lying flat and visible under the bed, photographed plainly with a generous area of empty calm surface across the lower half for the write on lines
must_show: the zone holding its standard
art.accept_test: The lower half of the frame must be visually quiet enough to print three blank lines over it and still read.

cards.title: GUEST NIGHTSTAND STANDARD
cards.tagline: WRITE IT. SIGN IT. PUT IT WHERE IT HAPPENS.
cards.objective: Lamp, two proven cables, tissues, coaster, wifi card. Nothing of the household's inside the drawer.
cards.trigger: When you make up the bed for an arrival, you switch the lamp on and charge your own phone from both cables before you leave the room.
cards.instruction: This is a write on card. Fill it in with a pen, in your own words if the printed sentence is not yours, and put it where the zone is. A standard nobody signed is a preference.
micro_quest: Wipe the lamp base and switch with a barely damp cloth so a guest's first touch in the dark is clean.
Vacuum the drawer's inside corners where dust settles behind the wifi card.
Test both charging cables against a real phone and note the date on a card inside the drawer.

art.subject: a bedside nightstand with a lamp switch within easy reach, one charging cable of each common type reaching toward the pillow, a coaster and a half-full tissue box on the surface, and an open drawer showing only a single wifi card inside, photographed plainly with a generous area of empty calm surface across the lower half for the write on lines
must_show: the zone holding its standard
art.accept_test: The lower half of the frame must be visually quiet enough to print three blank lines over it and still read.

cards.title: GUEST DRESSER STANDARD
cards.tagline: WRITE IT. SIGN IT. PUT IT WHERE IT HAPPENS.
cards.objective: Top two drawers empty and labeled reserved, lower drawers holding only spare linens for this room's bed, strap fixed to the wall.
cards.trigger: When you swap your own wardrobe over between seasons, you check the guest drawers are still empty before the swap counts as finished.
cards.instruction: This is a write on card. Fill it in with a pen, in your own words if the printed sentence is not yours, and put it where the zone is. A standard nobody signed is a preference.
micro_quest: Wipe the dresser top and the lamp or mirror on it until no smear remains.
Vacuum inside each empty top drawer before closing it, corners included.
Check the anti-tip strap's screws are still snug against the wall.

cards.title: GUEST CLOSET STANDARD
cards.tagline: WRITE IT. SIGN IT. PUT IT WHERE IT HAPPENS.
cards.objective: Six matching empty hangers past the tape line, a clear floor square for a suitcase, and every household bin lidded, labeled and below head height.
cards.trigger: When you fetch or return a seasonal bin, you count the six hangers before you close the door.
cards.instruction: This is a write on card. Fill it in with a pen, in your own words if the printed sentence is not yours, and put it where the zone is. A standard nobody signed is a preference.
micro_quest: Vacuum the closet floor corner behind where suitcases usually sit.
Wipe the rod itself with a dry cloth so a hanger slides on cleanly.
Check the taped guest-section line is still stuck down and readable.

art.subject: a guest closet with a clear stretch of rod holding six matching empty hangers past a strip of tape, an open floor square large enough for a suitcase, and a shelf of labeled lidded bins sitting below head height, photographed plainly with a generous area of empty calm surface across the lower half for the write on lines
must_show: the zone holding its standard
art.accept_test: The lower half of the frame must be visually quiet enough to print three blank lines over it and still read.

cards.title: GUEST WELCOME AND WORK SURFACE STANDARD
cards.tagline: WRITE IT. SIGN IT. PUT IT WHERE IT HAPPENS.
cards.objective: Clear desk, marked suitcase footprint, one labeled welcome bin with the ready-state photo inside the lid, and no cord crossing a walking line.
cards.trigger: When the guest's sheets go into the machine, the welcome bin is restocked and put back before you leave the room.
cards.instruction: This is a write on card. Fill it in with a pen, in your own words if the printed sentence is not yours, and put it where the zone is. A standard nobody signed is a preference.
micro_quest: Wipe the desk surface and lamp base with the neutral pH cleaner before the welcome bin goes back.
Vacuum the chair seat and the floor square marked for the suitcase.
Check the outlet and cord are still clear of the walking line.

art.subject: a guest room desk with a working lamp, a chair pulled up to it, a luggage rack beside a taped floor square, one labeled bin open to show a charger, wifi card, water glass and tissues, and a wall outlet with no cord crossing the floor, photographed plainly with a generous area of empty calm surface across the lower half for the write on lines
must_show: the zone holding its standard
art.accept_test: The lower half of the frame must be visually quiet enough to print three blank lines over it and still read.

cards.title: THE LATE-NIGHT ARRIVAL
cards.objective: A guest calls from the road an hour out, later than planned, and the bed has to be ready the moment they walk in.
cards.held_if: A complete set is already made up and the second set sits tagged and ready on the shelf, no laundry required.
cards.if_it_failed: If a set had to come out of the wash or off another bed first, the sustain trigger slipped. Draw GBA-001.
cards.instruction: Do not do anything to prepare. Live the day, then read the two lines below and be honest about which one you are.
cards.source: hand authored, not in the Manual

art.subject: a hand smoothing a finished, made-up guest bed at night with a tagged spare set visible folded on a nearby shelf
must_show: A guest calls from the road an hour out, later than planned, and the bed has to be ready the moment they walk in.
art.accept_test: The pressure has to be visible in the objects. No people's faces, so the load has to be shown by what is on the surfaces and, where unavoidable, by hands and feet alone.

cards.title: THE PHONE THAT NEEDS TO CHARGE OVERNIGHT
cards.objective: A guest's phone is nearly dead and they reach for whichever cable is on the nightstand without asking.
cards.held_if: Either cable on the nightstand charges the phone immediately, because both were tested this week.
cards.if_it_failed: If the cable did nothing, an untested one had drifted back into the drawer. Draw GBA-004.
cards.instruction: Do not do anything to prepare. Live the day, then read the two lines below and be honest about which one you are.

cards.title: THE WEEKEND GUEST WHO ACTUALLY UNPACKS
cards.objective: A guest staying more than one night opens the top drawers to unpack a full suitcase.
cards.held_if: Both top drawers are already empty and lined, ready for a full suitcase with nothing to clear out first.
cards.if_it_failed: If anything of the household's had to come out first, the reserved-drawer rule slipped. Draw GBA-005.

cards.title: THE COAT THAT NEEDS A HANGER IN THE DARK
cards.objective: A guest arrives after dark and reaches into the closet for a hanger without a light on.
cards.held_if: Six matching hangers are exactly where the tape line says they are, and the floor square underneath is clear to step onto.
cards.if_it_failed: If a hanger was missing or a bin was underfoot in the dark, the guest-section boundary slipped. Draw GBA-008.

cards.title: THE MORNING THE HOUSEHOLD'S OWN PROJECT SPILLS BACK IN
cards.objective: Someone needs the desk for the room's other job the same week a guest is due to arrive.
cards.held_if: The whole project clears into its one marked bin in a single trip, no unplugging required, leaving the desk clear.
cards.if_it_failed: If it took more than one trip or something needed unplugging, the marked footprint was never honestly set. Draw GBA-010.
